consensus_summary: Consensus identifies mercy primarily as God’s compassionate withholding of deserved judgment plus active lovingkindness (often paired with/distinguished from grace), with secondary senses in hesed/covenant loyalty, the mercy-seat typology, and required human compassionate practice.
book_summary: Book identifies mercy as covenant loyalty expressed through compassion, forgiveness, and faithful dealing, stressing that mercy received creates an obligation to show mercy and that pardon is joined to confession and forsaking.
consensus_core_identification: Divine compassionate non-retribution and lovingkindness (with human imitation)
book_core_identification: Covenant loyalty expressed as compassion/forgiveness/faithful dealing, conditioned on confession/forsaking and reciprocal obligation
boundary_disagreement: Book conditions mercy on confession/forsaking and treats received mercy as creating binding reciprocal obligation (Matt 18), whereas consensus commonly admits broader undeserved compassion without those covenant stipulations as definitional.
rationale: Consensus core (compassion that withholds punishment) remains intact as the book's acknowledged common view; book preserves that referent while materially tightening boundaries and conditions around covenant loyalty, reciprocal duty, and confession/forsaking. This is refinement of extension/precision, not replacement of the central category or a novel referent. Hesed/covenant loyalty already appears as a listed common alternative, so the shift is emphasis and boundary adjustment rather than contradiction or absence.
strongest_objection: One could argue the book simply elevates the already-common hesed alternative to primary status without truly narrowing the consensus core, making the relation closer to MATCH or COMPATIBLE_OVERLAP.
